### **2026-06-22 \- App VM Logging Demo Script (Publisher/Consumer)**

**Related Issues**: [\#51](https://github.com/MattToegel/it490-m2026-autopilot-engineers/issues/51), [\#52](https://github.com/MattToegel/it490-m2026-autopilot-engineers/issues/52), [\#53](https://github.com/MattToegel/it490-m2026-autopilot-engineers/issues/53), [\#54](https://github.com/MattToegel/it490-m2026-autopilot-engineers/issues/54) 

**Summary**: The demo script will call the App VM logging function from app\_log.php and send one test log event through RabbitMQ. This will help prove that the App VM can publish a log event to the MQ Server using the app.requests exchange and log.insert routing key. This issue presents the creation of  the API Worker Logging script. It ensures that logging messages are routed through RabbitMQ, it ensures that the log is labeled correctly with the criteria that match the database consumer, it converts the PHP into JSON in order for simple storage in the database, and it sends the message to RabbitMQ so it can be routed to the database log.

**Acceptance Criteria Check:**

* Publisher script is made to specifically route logging messages  
* Messages are noted to only be passing through RabbitMQ  
* Creation of Log should match the schematics of the DB consumer  
* Message should successfully be routed to the DB log through RabbitMQ  
* Comments are in the file in order to provide clarity  
* Log messages published and consumed successfully across VMs   
* Evidence: Review the Issues  
* PR: [\#60](https://github.com/MattToegel/it490-m2026-autopilot-engineers/pull/60)  
* Demo/Test Notes: N/A  
* Owner(s): Rosmy Antony (rma9), Xaidyn Liranzo (xml)

### **2026-06-23 \- Database Listener Script**

**Related Issue**: [\#57 Milestone 1 \- Create Database Listener Script](https://github.com/MattToegel/it490-m2026-autopilot-engineers/issues/57) 

**Summary**: Owner: Tristan Duncan  
UCID: tad46  
DB Server

Create the long-running, PHP, listener script on the db.logs queue for validation of incoming log messages. It should write valid ones to the MySQL logs table and route malformed messages to the dlq exchange. The consumer should also maintain a local mirrored log file. 

**Acceptance Criteria Check**:

* Script connects to RabbitMQ using credentials from the local .env file  
* Script connects to MySQL on the DB VM using credentials from the local .env file  
* Script listens continuously on the db.logs queue  
* Script validates each message has the required fields (source, level, message, created\_at)  
* Valid messages are inserted into the logs table in MySQL  
* Invalid or malformed messages are routed to the deadletter exchange and acknowledged  
* DB insert failures are also routed to the deadletter exchange  
* Each processed message is appended to a local mirrored log file (db\_listener.log)  
* DLQ routings are also recorded in the local log file for traceability  
* Script handles RabbitMQ connection failures gracefully with a clear error message  
* Script can be started with php logs\_consumer.php and runs until manually stopped  
* Evidence: [logs\_consumer.php](https://github.com/MattToegel/it490-m2026-autopilot-engineers/blob/main/db/logging/logs_consumer.php)  
* PR: [\#60](https://github.com/MattToegel/it490-m2026-autopilot-engineers/pull/60)  
* Demo/Test Notes: N/A  
* Owner(s): Tristan Duncan (tad46)

### **2026-06-24 \- DB VM User Registration with Hashed Password Storage**

**Related Issue:** [\#74](https://github.com/MattToegel/it490-m2026-autopilot-engineers/issues/74) 

**Summary:** Registration consumer stores bcrypt-hashed passwords on DB VM. 

**Acceptance Criteria Check:**

* auth\_consumer.php listens on the auth queue and handles both user.register and user.login routing keys

### **2026-06-25 \- App VM–MQ-Only Synchronization Verification**

**Related Issue:** [\#59](https://github.com/MattToegel/it490-m2026-autopilot-engineers/issues/59)

**Summary:** Verify that the App Server VM sends log events through RabbitMQ only, without using direct file copy, shared folders, rsync, SSH-based sync, HTTP calls, or direct database writes. This test checks the App VM logging scripts, confirms RabbitMQ port 5672 is reachable, and runs the App VM demo publisher to send a test log event through the MQ workflow.  

Acceptance Criteria Check:

* app\_log.php uses AMQPStreamConnection to connect to RabbitMQ.  
* app\_log.php publishes messages with basic\_publish.  
* App VM log events are sent to the app.requests exchange using the log.insert routing key.  
* Verification output shows no use of scp, rsync, file\_put\_contents, mysqli, PDO, HTTP calls, or direct log \- \[ \] syncing in the App VM logging scripts.  
* RabbitMQ port 5672 is reachable from the App VM.  
* No direct connections found outside RabbitMQ   
* Evidence:![][image4]  
* PR: [\#60](https://github.com/MattToegel/it490-m2026-autopilot-engineers/pull/60)

### **2026-07-20 \- User Registration Workflow**

**Related Issue:** [\#104](https://github.com/MattToegel/it490-m2026-autopilot-engineers/issues/104) 

**Summary:** Implement the App-side user registration workflow for the OnTheRadar MVP. This feature allows a new user to create an account through the browser interface. The App VM will validate user input, display appropriate success or error messages, and publish the registration request to RabbitMQ for processing by the Database VM.

**Acceptance Criteria Check:**

* User can enter a username, unique email address, and password to create an account.  
* Registration form validates required fields before submission.  
* Registration request is sent from the App VM through RabbitMQ.  
* User receives a success message when registration completes successfully.  
* User receives an appropriate error message if registration fails (e.g., duplicate email or invalid input).  
* The App VM does not communicate directly with the database during registration.  
* Evidence:![][image10]  
* PR: [\#105](https://github.com/MattToegel/it490-m2026-autopilot-engineers/pull/105)

### **2026-07-20 \- User Profile Management**

**Related Issue:** [\#120](https://github.com/MattToegel/it490-m2026-autopilot-engineers/issues/120)

**Summary:** Implement the user profile management feature to allow authenticated users to view and update their account information. Users should be able to view their username and role, update their email address, and change their password after confirming their current password. All profile update requests must be sent through RabbitMQ to the appropriate backend worker without direct database access from the App VM. 

**Acceptance Criteria Check:**

* Authenticated users can access the Profile/Settings page.  
* Users can view their username and role as read-only fields.  
* Users can update their email address.  
* Users can change their password by entering their current password, a new password, and confirming the new password.  
* The system displays appropriate success or error messages after profile update attempts.  
* Profile update requests are published to RabbitMQ for processing.  
* The App VM does not directly access or modify the database.  
* Updated profile information is displayed after a successful update.  
* Evidence:![][image12]

## **Milestone 3 \- Promotion Tool**

### **2026-08-02 \- Environment Lane Inventory & Readiness**
